newsitem.title: USA: Three children die in camper shell in California.
newsitem.headline: Three children die in camper shell in California.

text.p: A family trip ended in tragedy early on Monday when three young children sleeping in a camper shell behind a pickup truck died of suspected carbon-monoxide poisoning.

The three children, aged six and younger, were sleeping in a camper shell attached to a Nissan pickup truck as the family was returning from San Francisco, authorities said. When the family arrived at their home in North Hollywood the parents found the children were not breathing.

The parents had checked on the children shortly after 5.a.m. and all three children seemed fine, but by the time they arrived at their destination shortly after 6 a.m. all three had stopped breathing, authorities said.

Two of the children, Kevin, aged one year and nine months, and Kimberly, aged two years and nine months, were taken to The Children's Hospital of Los Angeles shortly after 6:30 a.m. and were pronounced dead shorthly after.

Kevin and Kimberly were not breathing and had no heart beat and attempts to recuscitate the pair failed, hospital spokesman Steve Rutledge said. The third child, 6-year-old Natalie, was taken to Cedars-Sinai Hospital and also died, authorities said.
"It is being treated as accidental," Los Angeles Police Department spokesman Arthur Holmes said.
"It appears to have been carbon monoxide poisoning that happened when they were travelling in a camper shell from up north. It happens all too often, it's just a tragedy," he said.
The parents, who were seated in the cab of the pickup, were not affected by the fumes. The journey from San Francisco to Los Angeles takes about seven hours.
The name of the family was withheld.
